chunks: Whatever breaks the wudu breaks the tayammum. Looking at water breaks the tayammum.

Whoever did tayammum and prayed, then found water while still in the time of prayer or after the time has passed, there is no repetition upon him, for the tayammum is one of the two purifications. So he is to do wudu for another prayer.

There is no harm in a person praying all the prayers of the night and day with a single wudu so long as he did not have a hadath. Likewise for the person with tayammum so long as he did not have a hadath or come upon water.
ai.seo_question: Does finding water after tayammum require repeating the prayer?
ai.summary: This legal ruling establishes key principles of tayammum (dry ablution with clean earth/dust), a substitute for wudu when water is unavailable. It clarifies that tayammum is an equally valid form of purification (one of the two tahurs), so prayers performed with it do not need to be repeated if water is later found. The ruling also confirms that both wudu and tayammum remain valid for multiple prayers as long as ritual purity (tahara) is not broken.
word_analysis: have a hadath (that which breaks purity)
for the one who did tayammum
